items.note: S1.1 states the net effect (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with restoration of scratch wires for arbitrary initial values, but omits that each invocation adds x_S to y_S via the eight-row schedule (copy included) and that the stages are forward/inverse/forward; it calls them 'three stages of gather, side-injection and scatter'. No derivation of the net map (JV+RG)x is given.

S1.2 gives the key idea (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so only endpoint operators remain) but not the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1} or the formula D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} / eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1} per route.

S1.3 states that labels from triples are nested nondegenerate subspaces whose only decreasing edges are central-wire edges, but gives no loss h per edge, no L=Ich, no budget Wm-2N+2L and no L<N/2 ('edge residuals are small' replaces the inequality).

S1.4 states the endpoint difference I_m on every role, the resulting shear H<-H+D and s_b<W_b m, which is the contract the interchange consumes; the exact formula s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b is omitted but nothing is misstated. No derivation from projections is given.

S1.5 states edge changes are products of kernels aI+bX_v telescoping to C^{tensor m} with s_c<W_c m, but omits that there is one kernel per orthonormal residual basis vector (which is what makes s_c the kernel count), the phase frame definition, and the diagonal corrections.
S1 and S1.6 state s<Wm and s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, but not the deficits eta_b, eta_c, their comparison with 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, or the source of the saving in L<N/2.

T2 covers digit/cyclic-row splitting, pointwise maps and merging in O(V) but omits digit permutations and moves; T3 states the controlled shift and unit scaling in O(V) but omits the condition that the offset be computable in b^{O(1)} time, and its phrasing blurs that the unit multiplier is a fixed rational, not control-dependent.

S3.1 states A=E_1 Pi E_2 with invertible lower triangular E_i and a partial permutation with a ones; S3.2 states exactly rank(A) interchanges of b-digit fields plus O(V) over Z/q^b. The proofs (1375-1392, 1412-1447) are not reproduced.

S3.3 states O(Ve^tau) for e=m^k and the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1); S3's method gives the paper's route (role streams, edge matrices via triangular factorization into rank-many recursive interchanges). Missing are the three-update conversion of the shear into an interchange (D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D) and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule costing O(V) per node.

S3.4 states the interchange (p,h,g,d,z)->(p,d,g,h,z) in O(Vu^tau) and names padding to power widths and base-m pieces; it omits how the row field is formed from rho=O(log e) high digits and padded to a multiple of W^k, and the padding of binary ranges to [q^e].

S4.1 paraphrases the paper's overview (C tensor products through smaller groups separated by binary changes of basis), and S4.3 mentions conversion to H_0, but the count of exactly s_c forward child calls on f=e/m axes, the conjugation by P_M, the inverse-child identity and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D are absent. Borderline with 'mentioned'.

S4.2 states XOR of corresponding selected bits with a restored third chunk, by a constant number of cyclic shifts plus sorting repair; the positions j_i=rho+iK, the bad fraction delta_bad and the cost O(V(L^tau+1)) are omitted.

S4's motivation only alludes to the rank saving applying to the layer; there is no recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), no row splitting among W roles, no leaf cutoff d^beta and no unrolling to d^{lambda'}.

S4/S4.3 state cost O(Vd^{lambda'}) and exact Gaussian-dyadic evaluation with one final truncation, but omit K=floor(d^c), the error bound sqrt2*2^{-p} and guard width. The method follows the paper's route (phase network, packed additions and chunk swaps, C to H_0) but skips the recursive row split and recurrence that produce the d^{lambda'} bound.

S5.1 correctly states omega_t=y^{2r/t}, contraction and F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I; S5.2 and S5's method give the common-offset layout. Missing are the bit-reversed decimation-in-frequency factorization into rounds, the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, the error sqrt2*l*2^{-p} and the explicit cost (S5 says only 'the stated cost').

S6.1 states signed Kronecker substitution at a power of two with the O(N log N) multiplier, but says one ring product is one integer product, whereas the paper makes four products of real/imaginary numerator evaluations at B_0=2^{4p}; output Q_p(fg/r) and cost O(rp log(rp)) are omitted.

S6/S6.2 follow the paper's route (two forward transforms kept in their common order, pointwise packed products, opposite transform), but omit the normalization (f*g)/(rM), the exact final scaling by M, the commutation P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), and the error and cost bounds.

S7.1 states P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA with the permutations kept inside, and S7.2 the tensor form RF_s=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A with linewise application; the hypothesis theta>p/alpha^4, the approximation errors and costs are omitted, and the Gaussian construction is not derived.

S7.3 says in words that QF_t u is a cyclic convolution with pointwise phases and that R cancels between forward and opposite transforms, but gives neither the chirp a_j nor the identities (permuted-chirp) and (u*v)/S^2.

S9 gives p=6b, d~b^epsilon, K~d^c, and S7 speaks of coprime lengths slightly below power-of-two lengths; the fixed rational values, T, r, l, alpha, gamma, and the existence and search of distinct primes in ((1-2eta)t_i,(1-eta)t_i] are absent.

S8.2 states the map x->prod x_i^{mu_i} carrying length-S convolution to coprime cyclic axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts; mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i, the triangular formula and the cost are not given.
S8.3 states x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r} turning cyclic wrap into negacyclic wrap mod y^r+1, which matches the paper; the M_C formula and error bounds are not given.

S8.4 lists the steps (coefficient map, two source transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, two scalings, rounding, carries) in the paper's order, but omits the scale factors S and 2^{2b+4}S, the input scaling 2^{-b-2}, Phi^{-1}, and the composition of the source transform from A, the chirp transform, B_0 and 2^gamma.
S8.5 states the final error is below 1/2 so rounding is exact, but gives none of the bounds (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-3b/4}) or the role of gamma<=b/4 and p=6b.

S9 states that every normalized cost term is at most p^{1-2kappa} giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), matching line 4983, but lists none of the table's terms or margins, the minimum margin g_2=2kappa, or the absorption of log factors and the schoolbook cutoff.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n conjecture, but does not state what an eventual lower bound means in the model or the liminf argument.

errors.says: Three stages of gather, side-injection and scatter send (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Each stage is an invocation of the eight-row schedule (subtract side injection and scatter, copy, gather, scatter, side injection, undo gather, undo copy); stages 1 and 3 are forward X to Y and stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X.

errors.says: The numerical layer has the same network structure as the address interchange, so the same rank saving applies to the layer.
errors.paper: The layer uses the complex construction (scalars in Z[i,1/2], even-intersection neighbours, extra central wire C_*) with its own s_c, W_c and exponent sigma, not the bit network used for the interchange; the saving is analogous, not the same.

errors.says: Signed Kronecker substitution makes one ring product an ordinary O(N log N) integer product.
errors.paper: Real and imaginary numerator polynomials are evaluated at B_0=2^{4p} and four integer products A_aA_c, A_bA_e, A_aA_e, A_bA_c are formed.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from stream primitives through the motif networks, interchange, simultaneous layer, synthetic transform and convolution, resampling and chirp, to the assembly and cost table. It thins out at the quantitative core: the label budget L=Ich<N/2 that makes s<Wm is never stated, the butterfly-layer recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) is missing, and the parameter/prime choices, error bounds and cost-table terms appear only as assertions, so the final p^{1-2kappa} bound is claimed rather than traced.
